## Overview

Enable MoRIIO WRITE for hybrid attention and Mamba/KDA models, including DSpark. This extends the hybrid READ support in #51052 and #57700 using existing transfer plans and post-draft save finalization.

## Claims

- Transfer attention KV, convolution and SSM state with per-group identity and completion accounting.
- Resolve the live final prefill state, exclude speculative scratch slots and publish matching N-1 token accounting.
- Use native `wait_all` with a finite deadline and a bounded fallback for older MoRI versions; nonblocking progress is unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased onto `642c18d64c`. The complete MoRIIO suite passed **274 tests**, followed by **3** block-state and **12** adjacent scheduler tests (**289 passed**). Changed Python files pass Ruff check and formatting. Full pre-commit installation was blocked by a certificate error while fetching actionlint.

```bash
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'hybrid or mamba or remote_kv or async_load or pending_push'
```

Real-weight GSM8K uses all 1,319 questions, concurrency 64, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42 and at most 256 output tokens.

| Validation | Control | Hybrid WRITE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current revision: Kimi-K3, TP8/DCP8, DSpark K4, block verification | Direct decode: 1,244/1,319 (94.31%) | Two runs: 1,232/1,319 (93.40%) and 1,253/1,319 (95.00%) |
| Previous revision: Kimi-Linear, TP2/DCP2, no speculation | READ: 1,167/1,319 (88.48%) | 1,171/1,319 (88.78%) |

Current K3 runs use connector revision `70c6fbfff9` on runtime `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, FP8 KV, FP32 recurrent state, A8W4, align-mode caching, GMU 0.90 and explicit P16/D40 GiB KV budgets per rank. The first full WRITE run imported 836,896 prompt tokens and recorded 67.86% real draft acceptance. Each full evaluation had one empty answer; the measurements show run-to-run variation, not bit-exact equivalence or a performance comparison. The previous Kimi-Linear evaluation used runtime `43b4aaea3`; it has not been repeated after this rebase.

```bash
uv run --no-project python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-tokens 256 --request-timeout-seconds 3600
```

The existing connector CI suite covers the unit tests. Distributed model evaluations were run separately.

Serving completed without engine termination or RDMA transfer failures. Prefill logged recoverable hipBLASLt fallback warnings; these runs are not a warning-free runtime qualification.

## Details

The three commits separate bounded completion waiting, grouped hybrid WRITE and DSpark support. Changes are confined to MoRIIO, its tests and its usage guide; no scheduler, model-runner, sampler or router implementation changes are needed.

1. Decode advertises allocated block IDs in transfer-group order.
2. Prefill resolves the live final slots and writes attention KV plus convolution and SSM state for the N-1 prompt.
3. Decode waits for all transfers before consuming the imported state and recomputing the final prompt token. A complete coupled local hit releases the producer without an empty remote load.

Set `read_mode: false` in both roles' `kv_connector_extra_config`, use matching cache layouts and TP sizes, and enable `--mamba-cache-mode align`. For DSpark, configure the same draft model on both roles. Sliding-window WRITE and other hybrid speculative methods remain unsupported. READ and plain-attention WRITE wire formats are preserved.

This adds hybrid recurrent-state WRITE, rather than duplicating attention registration work in #58585 or READ lifecycle work in #58968. The rebase retains upstream #57705 local-hit release and failure routing, per-layer registration geometry and one-shot receive guards.

+# matched, so correct transfers produce identical logits; this only absorbs the
+# fp32 rounding of the log-softmax (~1e-7), far below one bf16 logit step.

+# Several bf16 steps of the logits at DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE.
+MIN_CONTEXT_EFFECT = 0.05
+# Half-width of the uniform dummy init for 16/32-bit float weights, applied in
+# every server worker by moriio_wide_dummy.py. The loader default (1e-3) shrinks
+# every activation so far that a context change moves the first-token log-probs
+# by ~1e-4; at 0.1 it moves them by >0.1 and a corrupted prefill changes the
+# top-k set entirely.

+MAX_TOKENS = 4

+ALIGNED_BLOCKS = (1, 2)
+# Prefill chunks per long attention-only prompt, before the trailing token.
+ALIGNED_CHUNKS = (2, 4)

+def _graph_args(mode: str) -> list[str]:
+    if mode == "NONE":
+        return ["--enforce-eager"]
+    # Inductor otherwise picks reduction launch configs by timing them, so each
+    # separately compiled server may sum in a different order and drift by a
+    # few bf16 logit steps; deterministic mode fixes the choice.
+    config = {
+        "cudagraph_mode": mode,
+        "inductor_compile_config": {"deterministic": True},
+    }
+    return ["--compilation-config", json.dumps(config)]

+def _visible_devices() -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    selectors = ("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES")
+    selector = next((k for k in selectors if k in os.environ), selectors[0])
+    visible = os.getenv(selector)
+    devices = (
+        visible.split(",")
+        if visible
+        else [str(i) for i in range(current_platform.device_count())]
+    )
+    return selector, devices

+def _device_env(selector: str, device: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    # vLLM mirrors HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES into CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES at import, so
+    # the test process carries both; pin every selector or the server refuses
+    # the mismatch. ROCR narrows the set first, so HIP/CUDA then index into it.
+    env = {selector: device}
+    for key in ("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"):
+        if key != selector:
+            env[key] = "0" if selector == "ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES" else device
+    return env

+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _proxy(ping_port: int) -> Iterator[str]:
+    # Free ports for both sockets, so cases from parallel shards on one host
+    # do not collide.
+    port = get_open_port()
+    process = subprocess.Popen(
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            str(_PROXY),
+            "--port",
+            str(port),
+            "--service-discovery-port",
+            str(ping_port),
+        ],
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            assert process.poll() is None, "MoRIIO proxy exited during startup"
+            try:
+                requests.get(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/", timeout=1)
+                break
+            except requests.ConnectionError:
+                time.sleep(0.2)
+        else:
+            raise TimeoutError("MoRIIO proxy did not start")
+        yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
+    finally:
+        if process.poll() is None:
+            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
+            try:
+                process.wait(timeout=10)
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+                process.wait(timeout=10)
+

+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _pd_pair(
+    arch: ArchCase,
+    prefill_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    decode_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    case: Case,
+) -> Iterator[tuple[str, RemoteOpenAIServer]]:
+    selector, devices = _visible_devices()
+    assert len(devices) >= 2, "needs one GPU for prefill and one for decode"
+    prefill_port, decode_port, ping_port = (get_open_port() for _ in range(3))
+    with _proxy(ping_port) as proxy_url, contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+        servers: list[RemoteOpenAIServer] = []
+        stack.callback(RemoteOpenAIServer.shutdown_many, servers)
+        with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
+            futures = [
+                pool.submit(
+                    _server,
+                    arch,
+                    prefill_overrides,
+                    case.attention_backend,
+                    case.prefill_graph,
+                    devices[0],
+                    selector,
+                    port=prefill_port,
+                    extra_args=case.extra_args,
+                    kv_transfer_config=_moriio_config(
+                        "kv_producer", prefill_port, ping_port
+                    ),
+                ),
+                pool.submit(
+                    _server,
+                    arch,
+                    decode_overrides,
+                    case.attention_backend,
+                    case.decode_graph,
+                    devices[1],
+                    selector,
+                    port=decode_port,
+                    extra_args=case.extra_args,
+                    kv_transfer_config=_moriio_config(
+                        "kv_consumer", decode_port, ping_port
+                    ),
+                ),
+            ]
+            for future in futures:
+                servers.append(future.result())
+        _wait_for_registration(proxy_url, arch.model)
+        yield proxy_url, servers[1]
+
+
+def _wait_for_registration(proxy_url: str, model: str) -> None:
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        # The proxy hands decode max_tokens - 1 (prefill emits the first
+        # token), so the probe needs at least 2 for decode to accept it.
+        try:
+            response = requests.post(
+                f"{proxy_url}/v1/completions",
+                json={"model": model, "prompt": [1000, 1001], "max_tokens": 2},
+                timeout=300,
+            )
+            # The proxy streams the decode body, so a decode-side error can
+            # surface as a truncated response rather than a status code.
+            if response.status_code == 200 and response.json()["choices"]:
+                return
+        except requests.RequestException:
+            pass
+        time.sleep(1)
+    raise TimeoutError("prefill/decode never registered with the MoRIIO proxy")

+def _metric(server: RemoteOpenAIServer, name: str) -> list[Any]:
+    from prometheus_client.parser import text_string_to_metric_families
+
+    response = requests.get(server.url_for("metrics"), timeout=10)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return [
+        sample
+        for family in text_string_to_metric_families(response.text)
+        for sample in family.samples
+        if sample.name == name
+    ]

+def _block_size(server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> int:
+    # Hybrid models pad the attention block to the recurrent-state page, so the
+    # effective size is only known once the server has started.
+    sizes = {
+        int(sample.labels["block_size"])
+        for sample in _metric(server, "vllm:cache_config_info")
+    }
+    assert len(sizes) == 1, f"expected one cache block size, got {sizes}"
+    return sizes.pop()
+
+
+def _prompt_lengths(arch: ArchCase, server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> list[int]:
+    # Hybrid chunks end on cache-block boundaries; attention-only chunks end on
+    # the prefill budget, so the last token is computed on its own either way.
+    if arch.hybrid:
+        unit, counts = _block_size(server), ALIGNED_BLOCKS
+    else:
+        unit, counts = PREFILL_CHUNK, ALIGNED_CHUNKS
+    aligned = [
+        k * unit + 1 for k in counts if k * unit + 1 + MAX_TOKENS <= MAX_MODEL_LEN
+    ]
+    assert aligned, f"alignment unit {unit} leaves no aligned prompt"
+    return [SHORT_PROMPT_LEN, *aligned]
+
+
+def _prompts(lengths: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    return [[rng.randrange(1000, 30000) for _ in range(n)] for n in lengths]
+
+
+def _first_step(url: str, model: str, prompt: list[int]) -> dict[str, float]:
+    response = requests.post(
+        f"{url}/v1/completions",
+        json={
+            "model": model,
+            "prompt": prompt,
+            "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
+            "temperature": 0,
+            "logprobs": TOP_K,
+            "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
+        },
+        timeout=600,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    top = response.json()["choices"][0]["logprobs"]["top_logprobs"]
+    assert top, "server returned no logprobs"
+    return top[0]
+
+
+def _distance(ref: dict[str, float], got: dict[str, float]) -> float:
+    """Max difference of centered log-probs over the shared top-k tokens.
+
+    Centering removes the log-sum-exp offset, leaving the logit differences the
+    KV actually determines.
+    """
+    common = sorted(ref.keys() & got.keys())
+    if len(common) < len(ref) // 2:
+        return float("inf")
+    ref_mean = sum(ref[t] for t in common) / len(common)
+    got_mean = sum(got[t] for t in common) / len(common)
+    return max(abs((ref[t] - ref_mean) - (got[t] - got_mean)) for t in common)
+
+
+def _external_hits(server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> float:
+    samples = _metric(server, "vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total")
+    return sum(sample.value for sample in samples)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Reference:
+    prompts: list[list[int]]
+    logprobs: list[dict[str, float]]
+    hybrid: bool
+
+    @property
+    def expected_external_hits(self) -> int:
+        # Hybrid prefill stops one token short; attention-only prefill hands
+        # decode the whole prompt.
+        return sum(len(p) - int(self.hybrid) for p in self.prompts)
+
+
+def _reference(arch: ArchCase, overrides: dict[str, Any], case: Case) -> Reference:
+    """Direct serve; also checks that the comparison can see a wrong prefix."""
+    selector, devices = _visible_devices()
+    # Prefill graphs run the chunks and the decode-only last step runs the same
+    # captured graph in every decode mode used here, so the prefill mode
+    # reproduces both halves of the P/D computation.
+    with _server(
+        arch,
+        overrides,
+        case.attention_backend,
+        case.prefill_graph,
+        devices[0],
+        selector,
+        extra_args=case.extra_args,
+    ) as server:
+        url = server.url_root
+        lengths = _prompt_lengths(arch, server)
+        prompts = _prompts(lengths)
+        refs = [_first_step(url, arch.model, p) for p in prompts]
+        # Same tail, different early context: the comparison has to see it.
+        for prompt, ref in zip(prompts, refs):
+            altered = [t + 1 for t in prompt[: len(prompt) // 2]]
+            altered += prompt[len(prompt) // 2 :]
+            moved = _distance(ref, _first_step(url, arch.model, altered))
+            print(f"[sensitivity] len={len(prompt)} context-change distance={moved}")
+            assert moved >= MIN_CONTEXT_EFFECT, (
+                f"first-token log-probs barely depend on the context (moved "
+                f"{moved:.4g} for len {len(prompt)}); a wrong prefix would go "
+                "unnoticed"
+            )
